title: MIM World Model Calibration
goal: Teach MIM where things are in the workspace by building a temporary table/world coordinate model before attempting object pickup.
why: MIM can see objects and move the arm, but she does not yet reliably connect camera pixels, table coordinates, sensor readings, and joint movements into a usable world model.
boundary_rules: Do not start with pickup/grip attempts.
Do not treat marker positions as permanent; they are calibration references only.
Use slow, reversible movements from the saved safe exploration pose.
Capture visual/sensor evidence after each movement.
If camera view is occluded or C12/lidar status is unhealthy, pause and report what is missing.

phases.goal: Use four known table markers/corners to create a temporary coordinate frame.
actions: Place four visible markers on the table in a rectangle/square pattern
Capture hand camera, room camera, C12, and RPLIDAR from safe exploration pose
Label marker positions as A/B/C/D or equivalent
Record approximate pixel locations in hand camera and room camera
phases.success: MIM can describe table orientation and reference points without moving toward objects.

phases.phase: Phase 2 - Arm Pose To Workspace Mapping
phases.goal: Move gripper view toward each reference marker and record joint poses.
actions: Record pose and image at each marker alignment
Record how base/shoulder/elbow/hand changes affect image position
phases.success: MIM can explain which joints move the gripper left/right, nearer/farther, and up/down in the visible workspace.

phases.phase: Phase 3 - Hand Camera Visual Servo Baseline
phases.goal: Learn pixel offset between gripper center/tips and visible targets.
actions: Define gripper centerline in hand-camera image
Measure marker/object pixel offset from centerline
Verify expected direction of image change
phases.success: MIM can say target is left/right/near/far of gripper and choose a small correction move before contact.

phases.goal: Separate reference cards/markers/table edges from real interactable objects.
actions: Compare marker cards vs cube/block/ball visual traits
Create basic object candidate scoring: shape, height, color, contrast, marker exclusion
phases.success: MIM stops selecting marker cards as pickup objects unless the operator explicitly asks for a marker.

phases.goal: Score whether a grasp attempt is likely before closing the claw.
actions: Estimate object centeredness between claw tips
Check camera occlusion and table clearance
Predict likely success/failure and explain why
phases.success: MIM can refuse a bad close attempt and request/perform more alignment instead.

acceptance_criteria: MIM produces a workspace calibration artifact with table reference points and evidence images.
MIM records at least 8 movement samples from the safe exploration pose.
MIM explains observed movement effects in plain language.
MIM identifies at least one object candidate and at least one non-object reference/marker candidate.
MIM does not mark complete from a pickup attempt; completion requires calibration evidence.
